lines: A ring of 64 coupled cells running one of four physical simulations; two input probes push signal into the ring at a position you choose and two output probes read it back out.
The signal the left input probe pushes into the ring; a trigger here acts as a pluck and gives a struck, drum-like sound.
Moves the left input probe around the ring; the knob turns without end and the probe wraps round at the far side.
An attenuverter, -1 to +1, scaling the CV into the left input probe's position; at +1, 5V moves it a full lap.
Moves the left input probe around the ring, through the attenuverter above it.
Sets how wide an area of the ring the left input probe pushes on, 0.25 to 4; narrow is a pin, wide is a paddle.
An attenuverter, -1 to +1, scaling the CV into the left input probe's width.
Changes the width of the left input probe, through the attenuverter above it.
Sets the level of the left input before it reaches the ring, 0 to 8 on an exponential taper.
An attenuverter, -1 to +1, scaling the CV into the left input gain.
Changes the left input gain, through the attenuverter above it.
Cycles the shape of the left input probe: INTEGRAL, DIFFERENTIAL, SINC. The shape sets how the push is spread over the cells the probe covers.
Switches the left input between ADDITIVE, where its value is added to the ring, and MULTIPLICATIVE, where it is multiplied by the ring first, giving a ring modulation.
The signal the right input probe pushes into the ring; under RUNGE KUTTA RK4 it sets the speed and direction the contents of the ring rotate instead.
Moves the right input probe around the ring, turning without end. Under RUNGE KUTTA RK4 it is a bias on the rotation speed, applied whether or not anything is patched.
An attenuverter, -1 to +1, scaling the CV into the right input probe's position; at +1, 5V moves it a full lap.
Moves the right input probe around the ring, through the attenuverter above it.
Sets how wide an area of the ring the right input probe pushes on, 0.25 to 4. Under RUNGE KUTTA RK4 it multiplies the rotation speed and its bias instead.
An attenuverter, -1 to +1, scaling the CV into the right input probe's width.
Changes the width of the right input probe, through the attenuverter above it.
Sets the level of the right input before it reaches the ring, 0 to 8 on an exponential taper.
An attenuverter, -1 to +1, scaling the CV into the right input gain.
Changes the right input gain, through the attenuverter above it.
Cycles the shape of the right input probe: INTEGRAL, DIFFERENTIAL, SINC. Under RUNGE KUTTA RK4 it reads DISABLED and pressing it does nothing.
Switches the right input between ADDITIVE and MULTIPLICATIVE. Under RUNGE KUTTA RK4 it reads DISABLED and pressing it does nothing.
What the left output probe reads out of the ring, scaled by WET GAIN, with the left input scaled by DRY GAIN added to it.
Moves the left output probe around the ring, turning without end; this probe reads the ring rather than pushing on it.
An attenuverter, -1 to +1, scaling the CV into the left output probe's position; at +1, 5V moves it a full lap.
Moves the left output probe around the ring, through the attenuverter above it.
Sets how wide an area of the ring the left output probe averages over, 0.25 to 4; narrow reads one spot, wide reads a whole stretch.
An attenuverter, -1 to +1, scaling the CV into the left output probe's width.
Changes the width of the left output probe, through the attenuverter above it.
Cycles the shape of the left output probe: INTEGRAL, DIFFERENTIAL, SINC.
What the right output probe reads out of the ring, scaled by WET GAIN, with the right input scaled by DRY GAIN added to it.
Moves the right output probe around the ring, turning without end; this probe reads the ring rather than pushing on it.
An attenuverter, -1 to +1, scaling the CV into the right output probe's position; at +1, 5V moves it a full lap.
Moves the right output probe around the ring, through the attenuverter above it.
Sets how wide an area of the ring the right output probe averages over, 0.25 to 4.
An attenuverter, -1 to +1, scaling the CV into the right output probe's width.
Changes the width of the right output probe, through the attenuverter above it.
Cycles the shape of the right output probe: INTEGRAL, DIFFERENTIAL, SINC.
Steps through the four simulations in turn: WAVE EQUATION, SQUID AXON, SCHRODINGER, RUNGE KUTTA RK4.
Sets the size of the integration step and with it the pitch, marked in volts at 1V/octave with 0V near C4; the step is capped so it cannot pass the sample rate.
Sets the pitch at 1V/octave, added to the knob. This jack has no attenuverter and always passes in full.
Sets how far oscillations spread into neighbouring cells, 0 to 0.95, which calms a standing oscillation and smooths high frequencies out of the output.
An attenuverter, -1 to +1, scaling the CV into the damping.
Changes the damping, through the attenuverter above it.
Sets how quickly oscillations in the ring die away, 0 to 0.5; at 0 they ring on for a long time and give gong-like sounds.
An attenuverter, -1 to +1, scaling the CV into the decay.
Changes the decay, through the attenuverter above it.
Feeds each output probe back into the input probe on the same side, -8 to +8 with no feedback at the centre; negative feedback is inverted rather than weaker.
An attenuverter, -1 to +1, scaling the CV into the feedback.
Changes the feedback, through the attenuverter above it.
Sets a high-pass filter on the signal going into the ring, 0 to 1, which makes the result more plucked and less ringing.
An attenuverter, -1 to +1, scaling the CV into the low cut.
Changes the low cut, through the attenuverter above it.
Sets how much of the untouched input is added to the output, 0 to 8; it comes up at 0.
An attenuverter, -1 to +1, scaling the CV into the dry gain.
Changes the dry gain, through the attenuverter above it.
Sets the level of the signal read out of the ring, 0 to 8.
An attenuverter, -1 to +1, scaling the CV into the wet gain.
Changes the wet gain, through the attenuverter above it.
Note — Nothing is simulated until a cable is in one of the two output jacks. With both empty the ring is not updated at all and both outputs read 0V.
Note — Every CV attenuverter comes up at 0, so a cable in a CV jack does nothing until the small knob beside that jack is turned. TIME/1VOCT is the exception and has no attenuverter.
Note — DRY GAIN comes up at 0, so only the processed signal is heard until it is raised.
Note — With both inputs set to MULTIPLICATIVE the whole ring can settle to zero and stay there, since anything times zero is zero. Switching one input to ADDITIVE brings it back.
Note — Under RUNGE KUTTA RK4 the right input probe becomes a rotation control: POSITION/BIAS sets the base speed and direction, WIDTH/SPEED multiplies it, and the two buttons under it read DISABLED.
Note — The display draws the state of the ring, the four probe positions and the model in use, and under RUNGE KUTTA RK4 a dial for the rotation. Nothing on it can be clicked.
Note — These simulations are unstable by design and can squeal, ring or get very loud, especially with FEEDBK raised. Soft clipping keeps it recoverable rather than preventing it.
Menu — Oversampling mode: Sinc, Biquad — chooses how the input, feedback and output paths are filtered; Biquad is the setting a new module takes.
Menu — Internal clip range: 10V, 30V, 60V, 100V — sets the ceiling the soft clipping inside the simulation works to; 30V is the setting a new module takes.

FreeSurface-WaterTable.notes:
Read at commit 69231f3, 'Bump version number'. It is the only commit in the repository whose plugin.json carries 2.1.4 and it is HEAD, so nothing needed settling against the binary.

The ring is 16 float_4 vectors, 64 cells, closed end to end (src/WaterTable.cpp:16-17, MAX_POSITION at :20 is 64). The four probes come up evenly spaced round it: left input at 0, left output a quarter of the way round, right input at the half and right output at three quarters (src/WaterTable.cpp:1058-1061).

Every parameter with a CV jack goes through CVParamInput, which configures a -1 to +1 attenuverter defaulting to 0 (src/CVParamInput.hpp:38-43) and rescales the jack from ±5V to ±1 (:161). That is why every CV input on this panel is inert out of the box. The one exception is TIME/1VOCT, declared with DUMMY_CV so its multiplier is a fixed 1.0 (:163-164) and the jack tracks 1V per octave in full.

The position knobs are declared -HUGE_VALF to +HUGE_VALF (src/CVParamInput.hpp:58) and drawn as endless knobs, and the value is taken modulo the ring, so there are no end stops and no wrong position.

The whole simulation is inside a test for either output being connected (src/WaterTable.cpp:1170). With both outputs empty setParams, setProbeInputs and update are never called, so the ring is frozen, and the dry path is written inside per-output isConnected tests as well.

The README says WaterTable 'does not use digital delays or reverbs' and calls the design fully analog. What the code runs is a Runge-Kutta 3/8 integration of a 64-cell difference scheme at a controllable timestep, with biquad or sinc oversampling on the input, feedback and output paths (src/WaterTable.cpp:340-360). The claim is about the modelling approach, not about the implementation, and nothing in the lines repeats it.

The README's Alternative Mode section says the right input probe's pattern controls are 'disabled' under Runge-Kutta. The buttons are not merely ignored: both of them read DISABLED on the panel and their toggle lambdas are wrapped in an isModMode test (src/WaterTable.cpp:1416 and :1446), so the button can be clicked and will not change anything. They are tagged and their lines say so.

Nineteen lights carry the shape and mode readouts and the output level. They are lights, not params, so they have no census position and no click reaches them; what they show is said in the lines for the buttons they sit beside.

DRY GAIN is the only knob in the module whose default is the bottom of its range (src/WaterTable.cpp:1075), which is why a new module is entirely wet.

Damping and the model equations use the term diffusion rather than the usual audio meaning of damping; the README says so and the line is written to the behaviour rather than to the word.
